---
title: "Toy adaptive-dynamics models in regnans"
---
::: {.eyebrow}
theory
:::

Per-model write-ups of the fast toy adaptive-dynamics models shipped with
[`regnans`](https://github.com/traitecoevo/regnans). Each model has an
explicitly-coded invasion fitness and equilibrium (backed by C++), so it runs in
milliseconds and has known answers to validate the assembly / attractor
algorithms against — a complement to the full `plant` SCM. They pair with the
[adaptive dynamics](../adaptive-dynamics.qmd) theory page, which develops
invasion fitness for the full size-structured model.

Each page gives a brief description of the original paper, the fitness equations,
and a worked example using the `regnans` harness API.

| Model | Paper | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| [DD99](DD99.qmd) | Dieckmann & Doebeli 1999 | competition kernel; branching iff $\sigma_C<\sigma_K$ |
| [GK98](GK98.qmd) | Geritz, Kisdi, Meszéna & Metz 1998 | soft selection; branching iff $d/\sigma>\sqrt{3/2}$ |
| [GM99](GM99.qmd) | Geritz, van der Meijden & Metz 1999 | seed size in safe sites; branching at high asymmetry |
| [JJ12](JJ12.qmd) | Johansson & Jonzén 2012 | bird arrival time; a single CSS, $x^\*=x_{opt}-a\sigma^2$ |

All single-model pages use the same pipeline:

```r
library(regnans)
h <- harness_dd99()                                   # or _gk98 / _gm99 / _jj12
community_start(bounds(x = c(-2, 2)), harness = h) |>
  community_solve_singularity_1D()                    # -> evolutionary attractor
```

The DD99, GK98 and GM99 models also handle **mixtures**, so beyond pairwise
invasibility plots you can run the full community-assembly algorithm and watch a
multi-species community build up by branching and limiting similarity — including
**DD99 in two trait dimensions**. See [Community assembly](assembly.qmd).

> Rendering these pages requires `regnans` (and its dependency `plant`) to be
> installed, not just loaded from source.
